newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki manages new highs, Nokia strong.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki manages new highs, Nokia strong.

text.p: After a mixed start shares heaved to new highs in thin summer trade on Monday, helped by a late uptick in Nokia and with a higher opening on Wall Street pointing the way to continued strength, brokers said.
The FOX index gained 0.24 percent to end at 1,150.46 points, its fifth straight record close, while the all-share HEX added 0.34 percent to 3,344.66.
"The U.S. market opened strongly, so things here look good," one broker said, after the Dow industrials gained more than 50 points at the start, triggering curbs on trading.
Nokia was helped by news late in the session of growing support for its joint wireless protocol for mobile phones and by brisk overseas demand, especially from the U.S.
After a firm opening in New York, brokers said Nokia looked set to stay in its new trading range above 400.00 markka -- a hurdle it cleared for the first time on Friday.

Banking group Merita gained 0.10 markka in lively 28 million markka volume to close back up at 20.00, but brokers said there were still plenty of sellers at that level. "Twenty markka looks like a tough barrier," one said.
UPM-Kymmene pulled the forestries subindex higher.
It put on 0.60 markka to close at 127.50 after moderate 17 million markka dealings. Enso ended flat at 49.30, and Metsa-Serla fell 0.80 markka to 45.00 in thin volume.

National carrier Finnair ended up 0.50 markka at 37.50 after touching 38.50 in hefty 17 million markka volume. Several big blocks matched in-house at Merita at 37.30-37.50/share accounted for most of the volume.
Brokers either declined comment or could give no clear reason for the activity in Finnair: some said slightly higher May passenger load figures had nothing to do with the gains.
